name: ClientCosmeticsTickSystem (Chroma keyboard lighting + option-driven toggles)
summary: Game-EA per-frame client helper. Pushes the local player's hero colour to the Razer Chroma keyboard-LED manager (6x22 key grid). Also counts down a timer in lobby comp 0x50, and enables or disables per-entity feature objects according to the user's option bytes.
tick: 1) Anti-tamper rdtsc check (ignore). 2) lobbyEA comp 0x50 (singleton, 0x720 bytes, profile/options) +0x144 -= dt, clamped at 0. 3) FUN_7ff650bfcd40: gets the LED manager via (*DAT_7ff6517fe448)->vfunc+0x2b8, gets the colour vec4 at +0x168 of the local player's comp 0x3F -> hero data (FUN_7ff650bfcc00, falls back to a default colour), packs it to RGBA8 at mgr+0x454, sets the dirty flag and ticks the manager (FUN_7ff650893560, which calls the SDK fnptr with (2, int[6][22]). 4) FUN_7ff650bfce30: if the EA is a game EA, walks the handle list in singleton comp 0x5E (count +0x20). It resolves each handle via FUN_7ff650cc3f60 (entity-id + index -> object in the entity's 0x1e0 list) and reads option id +0x130 against the lobby comp 0x50 option bytes (+0x2ce / +0x454 [profile*0xc3 + id]). It then calls FUN_7ff650ce5bc0 (enable, +0x134=1) or FUN_7ff650ce5c90 (disable, +0x134=0).
callbacks: OnInitialize (not defined in Ghidra, 0x7ff650bfcae0) registers {callback 0x7ff650bfcaa0, this} into global object [0x7ff6517fe458]+0x730/+0x738. PreDelete (0x7ff650bfcb00) clears them.
interacts_with: Razer Chroma LED SDK wrapper (DAT_7ff6517fe448 vfunc+0x2b8)

key_functions.0x7ff650bfcd40: update LED colour from local hero
key_functions.0x7ff650893560: LED manager tick; calls SDK fn(2, 6x22 colour grid)
key_functions.0x7ff650bfce30: option-gated enable/disable of objects listed in comp 0x5E

evidence: The 6x22 int grid of packed RGBA passed to a function pointer is the Chroma keyboard layout. The colour comes from hero data at +0x168. It is created first in FUN_7ff650bde670 (game EA construction) as a 0x10-byte object with vtable 0x15a23a8.

name: PvpSystem (PvP game-state notifier / match-end watcher)
summary: Each tick it looks at the PvPGame singleton (comp 0x24). While its +0xc0 counter is above zero it broadcasts change flag 0x2000000 through the EA's world-change notifier and decrements the counter. When a certain system's state byte equals 7 (likely match finished), it runs an end-of-game path that sets a flag on that system.
tick: comp 0x24 = FUN_7ff650c386f0(EA) (iteration list +0x360). If +0xc0 > 0: notifier = EA->vfunc+0x80(); notifier->vfunc+0x10(0x2000000); comp+0xc0--. Anti-tamper rdtsc. sys = first EA system assignable to type 0x7ff6517986a8 (FUN_7ff650bfc790). If *(u8*)(sys+0x10)==7, run FUN_7ff650bfb930. That function contains anti-debug timing junk, looks up the system of type 0x7ff6517987a8 and follows +0x10 vfunc -> +0x3a8, looks up hash DAT_7ff651756f00 in a map, checks the local player component (FUN_7ff650c3be10), then sets sys+0x52 = 1.
interacts_with: EA world-change notifier (EA vfunc+0x80, same one used by StatescriptSystem 0x15c2e20)
server_relevance: probably client-side reaction to server-replicated PvP state. The server owns PvP state itself.
evidence: The +0x360 iteration list is comp 0x24. The 0x2000000 notification uses the same EA vfunc+0x80 notifier interface that FUN_7ff650c10560 uses for component-change flags. The purpose of state 7 was not confirmed.

name: SpectateTargetSystem
summary: Chooses the entity the local client is viewing or spectating and tells the server. If the local player has no own view target (or the game is in state 7 / spectator mode), it sends the chosen entity id through the EA message channel at EA+0x1d0. An option (lobby comp 0x50 byte +0x331) makes it cycle to the next candidate entity.
tick: Anti-tamper page CRC check (ignore). Calls an optional callback at +0x20(+0x28), then FUN_7ff650c55460. That function reads the local entity id (FUN_7ff650c3c3e0 -> +0x94) and the current view/camera target id (FUN_7ff650c3cf10). If (lobby state == 7 or FUN_7ff650c3db10) and the local id is valid and there is no view target, it calls the +0x10 callback with the local id. If the auto-cycle option byte is set, FUN_7ff650c558b0 instead picks the next id from a sorted candidate list (FUN_7ff651032e50: next after the current spectated id) and passes that to the callback.
callbacks: OnInitialize (0x7ff650c54d70, not in Ghidra) sets +0x10 = FUN_7ff650c56db0 and +0x18 = this. FUN_7ff650c56db0 builds a message (vtable 0x7ff6515efe98) carrying the entity id and sends it via EA+0x1d0 (vfunc0 = can-send, vfunc1 = send).

key_functions.0x7ff650c55460: choose target and invoke send callback
key_functions.0x7ff651032e50: next entity id after the current one in the sorted candidate list

server_relevance: client->server notification. A server should accept or ignore this 'view target' message; the system itself is client-only.
evidence: Entity-id handling with invalid sentinel DAT_7ff65183a0c8 / 0x1fffffff masks. The cyclic 'next id' search over a sorted list. The callback posts a message object through EA+0x1d0.

name: PhysicsAreaRegistrySystem (gravity/dampening areas + character movers)
summary: When an entity with a DampeningArea (0x09), GravityArea (0x0A) or CharacterMover (0x15) is added, this system either records the area entity's handle in a map keyed by the area's component data, or registers the mover's transform with the scene/physics world.
callbacks: OnEntityAdded (0x7ff650feda80). If comp 0x09: key = own vfunc 14 (FUN_7ff650c02c40 = get comp 9)+8, map[key] = entity+0x90 handle. If comp 0x0A: key = vfunc 15 (FUN_7ff650c02cd0 = get comp 10)+0x20, map[key] = handle. If comp 0x15: FUN_7ff6509e6e90 -> FUN_7ff6509d2a50(scene = comp0x01+0x198, transform comp 0x01, add=1), which adds the transform to the scene's dynamic list at +0xb0 (deferred if the scene is locked). OnInitialize reserves a 16-slot map at +0x10. PreDelete frees the map. No remove callback.
server_relevance: server-side game logic: gravity and dampening areas affect movement, and the server simulates movement
evidence: Subscriptions 0x09/0x0A/0x15 and entity mask bit tests for 9, 10 and 21 (0x15). Uses entity handle +0x90. Scene +0x198 dynamic list.

name: StatescriptSystem (world-change notifier / instance teardown, game variant)
summary: Statescript-side system in the game EA. It registers component add/remove watchers and turns those changes plus entity create/delete of comp 0x0E entities into invalidation flags on the EA's world-change notifier (EA vfunc+0x80). Statescript target queries use these flags to re-evaluate. Its slot-6 teardown destroys every Statescript instance.
callbacks: OnEntityCreated/OnEntityDeleting (FUN_7ff65100ff70, shared with lobby 0x15c4a08): skip projectiles (comp 0x27) whose STU flag +0xf1 is false; otherwise notify(1), and also notify(0x80) if entity+0xa0 bit0. OnInitialize (FUN_7ff650c10410 -> FUN_7ff650c105c0) registers FUN_7ff650c10560 on the EA+0x198 component-event dispatcher for comps 0x28 (flag 2), 0x20 (4), 0x13 (8), 0x3D (0x10), 0x3E (0x20), 0x10 (0x40), 0x40 (0x80), 0x3F (0x100). Slot 6 (FUN_7ff650c10440) walks all comp 0x23 and calls FUN_7ff650f24120 on the sync manager (+0xc0), which destroys all instances ('Instance destructor called from teardown').
server_relevance: server-side game logic: Statescript target and filter invalidation is needed wherever Statescript runs
evidence: The watched component set (health, team filter, target tag, player info, pet) is what target selection depends on. The teardown string. The lobby twin 0x15c4a08 shares callbacks and ticks Statescript. Note: the brief says 'System 43' spawns map entities during map load; that was not seen in the slots examined.

name: MovementFlagEffectSystem (spawns an attached local effect entity on a movement-state flag edge)
summary: Iterates the MirroredAnim components (0x1C) on entities that have MovementState (0x12). When bit 0x4 of the movement flags at +0x198 rises, it spawns a local entity from definition 0x03000000000007AB in the entity's scene and parents that entity's transform to the owner. Each tick it also drains an object pool free list.
tick: FUN_7ff650be80d0: while DAT_7ff6517fd788+0xe4 > 1, pop the free list (FUN_7ff6507d9b40) and release into DAT_7ff651872130. Anti-tamper checks. For each comp 0x1C where the entity has comp 0x12: FUN_7ff650cada50 edge-detects the MovementState+0x198 bit 4 against the cached +0x14a0. On a rising edge it calls FUN_7ff6509d33f0(scene, 0x3000000000007ab, ...) to spawn, FUN_7ff6509d2290 to add, then FUN_7ff6509e1070 to attach the new transform to the owner transform.

key_functions.0x7ff650cada50: flag-edge detect and spawn attached entity 0x7ab

server_relevance: likely client-only visuals, since a locally spawned attached entity is typically an effect
evidence: Iteration list +0x2a0 = comp 0x1C. Mask bit 0x12 check. Entity-definition GUID 0x03000000000007AB (not resolved). Transform attach.

name: PlayerStatsMessageHandlerSystem (game EA)
summary: Stateless system with no ECS callbacks. It is a type-tagged host for incoming messages: handlers look it up by type (FUN_7ff650c4a1c0) and dispatch message ids 0x6A40 (hero stats dump 'Total Hero Stats' / 'Stats for Hero'), 0x6A41 ('Total Player Map Stats') and 0x6A42 (profile update via FUN_7ff650c24f80 -> FUN_7ff650cc9200). Any other id is a protocol error and closes the connection.

key_functions.0x7ff650c4a1c0: find this system in the EA (type 0x7ff651798478)

server_relevance: server->client stats and profile messages. The server may send them; the client-side system itself is trivial.
evidence: The vtable overrides only type info and dtor. Typeinfo 0x7ff651798478 is used by FUN_7ff650c4a1c0, which the message handlers FUN_7ff650c481a0 and FUN_7ff650c51140 call. Strings in the handlers name the stats.

name: GameSoundSystem (listener + sound importance)
summary: Game audio driver. Each tick it places the audio listener at the current camera / view-target entity. It then ranks hero sound sources by importance into high/medium/low tiers using a sound-config STU, and pushes audio option settings to the audio engine.
tick: Listener entity (+0x28 id) has comp 0x0C: FUN_7ff650a3e4d0(comp0x0C, view-target handle). EA vfunc+0xe8 -> camera +0x40 -> FUN_7ff6509e45c0 sets the listener transform. FUN_7ff650c8ef50(dt) runs the importance pass: reset comp 0x21 +0x20, add per-player weights (list from FUN_7ff650c36ec0, +0x138), iterate comp 0x20 entities that have comp 0x21, score them (FUN_7ff650c8fdd0), sort, compute mean and stddev, and assign tiers 0/1/2 using config counts +0x40/+0x44/+0x48 and thresholds +0x50/+0x54. Then, depending on lobby comp 0x50 option bytes +0x2d5/+0x390, it calls audio engine DAT_7ff6517fe430 vfuncs +0x110/+0x120 and +0x148.
callbacks: OnInitialize (FUN_7ff650c8e1f0) sets +0x50 = STU ref 0x0CA0000000000069 (sound importance config) and registers cvars sound_DrawSound, sound_ForceImportance ('Force importance') and sound_AllowMultipleHighImportance. PreDelete at 0x7ff650c8e650.
evidence: Strings 'Draw sound importance', sound_DrawSound, sound_ForceImportance and sound_AllowMultipleHighImportance. Iteration lists +0x300 (0x20) and +0x318 (0x21). Audio engine vtable calls.

name: EffectPhysicsSystem (job-parallel simulated effect bodies)
summary: Owns singleton comp 0x57, which holds two 0x110-byte-per-entry object arrays and two spatial broadphase grids. Each frame it runs worker-thread jobs over these entries, writes the resulting transforms back to their entities, and handles sphere-overlap queries, bone attachment, and collision/lifetime state on the entities' Effect component (0x0D).
tick: comp 0x57 = FUN_7ff650c36380(EA). If scene+0x3e9 is set, flush and destroy dead entries. Merge ranges (FUN_7ff650c9d800). Lock scene (+0x3f0++). Dispatch jobs over the +0x20 and +0x38 arrays through the TLS job system FUN_7ff6507d97d0. Per entry, FUN_7ff650c993f0 writes the transform (FUN_7ff6509e4000/45c0), sets comp 0x0D +0xd4 state 0..3, checks broadphase overlap (FUN_7ff650c98c50 over grids +0x58/+0x60) and, on hit, sends event 0xF2 to comp 0x03. For the second array, FUN_7ff650c9b040 handles bone attach (FUN_7ff650a190f0), sphere query on scene+0x3a0 with callback FUN_7ff650c9aab0, parenting, and optional spawn/destroy. Unlock the scene; FUN_7ff650c98090 does cleanup.
callbacks: OnEntityAdded (0x7ff650c9d500): allocates two 0xe0-byte broadphase grids (FUN_7ff650c97990) into comp0x57+0x58/+0x60. OnEntityRemoved (0x7ff650c9d600): frees them.
server_relevance: probably client-only (drives comp 0x0D effects); confirm before discarding
evidence: Mask word +0xa0 bit 23 = comp 0x57. Mask bit 13 = comp 0x0D (STUEffectComponent). Parallel job dispatch. AABB grid code. Event 0xF2 on collision.

name: EmptyServiceSystem (stateless tag)
summary: 0x10-byte system that overrides only type info and dtor. In FUN_7ff650bde670 it is registered in the same 'service' group (type 0x7ff6517984b8) as several non-system managers. No code references its typeinfo 0x7ff651799558 other than its own vtable.
evidence: Every vtable slot is a shared default except type info (0x7ff650c54bc0..) and dtor. The only xrefs to its type are from its own vtable.

name: BattleNetConnectionSystem (lobby login-server connection)
summary: Lobby-EA client for the login/lobby service connection. It parses host:port (default port 3724; configured value '127.0.0.1:3724'), uses the account name ('steamuser'), runs a connect state machine with timeouts, and drains the received-message queue every tick.
tick: State +0x50: in state 0, if the vfunc 14..17 predicates (lobby EA+0x1a0 flags, EA+0x178 state==0x10) allow, connect (FUN_7ff6510c1920 -> FUN_7ff6510c1ba0 resolves host:port, then FUN_7ff6510c2050). Timeouts reset via FUN_7ff6510c19a0: state 1 >5 s, any state except 6 >60 s, state 5 >5 s. It always calls FUN_7ff6510c2320, which pops the message list under a critical section (+0x210) and handles each (FUN_7ff6510c23f0).
callbacks: OnInitialize (0x7ff650c65450 -> FUN_7ff6510c16c0) stores the host string and allocates socket and buffer objects (FUN_7ff6513395f0, FUN_7ff651339a10). PreDelete (FUN_7ff6510c17d0) tears them down and disconnects.
server_relevance: client side of the login/lobby server link. The server must implement the peer protocol on port 3724.
evidence: Default port 0xE8C = 3724. Live strings at RVA 0x18ac010 '127.0.0.1:3724' and 0x18abf10 'steamuser' (via vtable slots 20/23). QPC and 5 s/60 s timeouts.

name: VoiceChatSystem (Vivox)
summary: Lobby-EA voice chat manager built on Vivox. It reads voicechat_* cvars, sets the Vivox server URL, runs the login/channel state machine, and applies speaker volume, mic volume and push-to-talk / VAD settings.
tick: Unless voicechat_forceDisable is set: iterates channel participants from the profile singleton (FUN_7ff650c24f80, FUN_7ff650d2f430) and mutes by option (lobby comp 0x50 +0x378). Defaults the server to https://owp.www.vivox.com/api2 / owp.vivox.com. Drives state +0xb0 (login 3->5, join 6->8, 9->7, etc.) via FUN_7ff650d30xxx. Applies voicechat_volume and micVolume (audio engine vfunc +0xc0) and VAD thresholds. Ends with FUN_7ff650d2f020(dt).
callbacks: OnInitialize (FUN_7ff650c659a0) registers cvars voicechat_forceEnable, forceDisable, forceLogin, volume, micVolume, vadHangoverMS, vadThreshold, activeSpeakingThreshold and inactiveSpeakingThreshold. PreDelete at 0x7ff650c66de0.

name: ProfileUnlocksMessageHandlerSystem (lobby EA)
summary: Stateless lobby system. It is a type-tagged host for incoming profile/unlock messages 0x5EEC–0x5EF0: profile/unlock data via FUN_7ff650c24f80 -> FUN_7ff650cc8770/88d0/8a10, 0x5EEE to FUN_7ff650c28dc0 + 0x40, 0x5EEF 'Default Unlocks', and 0x5EF0. Unknown ids close the connection.
server_relevance: lobby server->client profile/unlock messages that the server should send; the system itself is trivial
evidence: Only type-info and dtor slots are overridden. Typeinfo is used by FUN_7ff650c49d90, which handler FUN_7ff650c47fa0 calls. The 'Default Unlocks' string.

name: StatescriptSystem (lobby variant)
summary: Lobby-EA twin of the game StatescriptSystem 0x15c2e20. It shares the create/delete notifier callbacks and the slot-6 teardown. It also has an extra method that advances every Statescript component using wall-clock time.
tick: No OnTick slot. Vfunc 14 (FUN_7ff650c7ac50, reached through the secondary base at this-0x10) iterates comp 0x23. For each one with +0x419 set it calls syncmgr(+0xc0)->vfunc+0x1c8(round(time*1000)), i.e. advances Statescript to the current time in ms.
callbacks: OnEntityCreated/OnEntityDeleting = FUN_7ff65100ff70 (notify flags 1/0x80 for comp 0x0E entities, as in 0x15c2e20). Slot 6 = FUN_7ff650c10440 (destroy all Statescript instances). OnInitialize is the default, so no component-change watchers are registered.

key_functions.0x7ff650c7ac50: advance all Statescript comps by time (ms)

server_relevance: lobby UI Statescript; not needed for match serving
evidence: Its vtable shares slots 6, 8, 10 and 11 with 0x15c2e20. Iteration +0x348 = comp 0x23. syncmgr vfunc+0x1c8 is called with a millisecond value.
